themes_detail.label: Dead Animals & Carcasses Spike
themes_detail.summary: Dead animal complaints surged to 8 this week, a 611% spike versus the 1.1 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 5.42), signaling a potential public health or wildlife management crisis in Park Slope/Carroll Gardens this week.
evidence: 8 dead animal complaints filed THIS WEEK vs. 1.1 weekly baseline over prior 8 weeks
Z-score of 5.42 indicates statistically significant anomaly
611% increase from baseline suggests acute event or condition, not gradual trend
reporting_angles: Contact NYC Sanitation and Parks Dept to identify cause: wildlife die-off, disease outbreak, or environmental hazard?
Interview residents about what they've observed; geo-tag complaints to identify hotspot blocks

themes_detail.label: Bike Rack Infrastructure Complaints
themes_detail.summary: Bike rack complaints jumped to 5 this week, a 1233% spike from the 0.4 weekly average (z-score: 6.65), suggesting rapid deterioration of cycling infrastructure or sudden demand for new racks in the district this week.
evidence: 5 bike rack complaints filed THIS WEEK vs. 0.4 weekly baseline over prior 8 weeks
Z-score of 6.65 indicates extreme statistical deviation
1233% increase suggests either infrastructure failure or unmet demand
reporting_angles: Obtain 311 complaint details: are residents reporting damaged racks, insufficient racks, or obstruction?
Interview cyclists about what prompted the spike; check if new development or street work triggered complaints

themes_detail.label: Street Signage Damage Surge
themes_detail.summary: Damaged street sign complaints reached 6 this week, a 700% increase from the 0.8 weekly average (z-score: 5.42), indicating widespread street furniture deterioration or vandalism across Park Slope/Carroll Gardens this week.
evidence: 6 street sign complaints filed THIS WEEK vs. 0.8 weekly baseline over prior 8 weeks
Z-score of 5.42 indicates statistically significant spike
700% increase suggests acute damage event (weather, vehicles, vandalism)
reporting_angles: Contact NYC DOT to determine if weather event, traffic incident, or systematic vandalism caused damage
Visual inspection of major intersections (Prospect Park West, Flatbush, Carroll Street) to map damage

themes_detail.label: Building Code Violations Accelerating
themes_detail.summary: Building/Use violations surged to 7 complaints this week, a 522% spike from the 1.1 weekly average (z-score: 6.34), suggesting either enforcement activity, illegal conversions, or zoning violations emerging in the district this week as multiple ULURP rezonings and 1,018 building permits remain in pipeline.
evidence: 7 Building/Use violations filed THIS WEEK vs. 1.1 weekly baseline over prior 8 weeks
Z-score of 6.34 indicates extreme statistical deviation
1,018 building permits on file (641 alterations, 122 new buildings) suggest active construction and potential code conflicts
46 Nelson Street rezoning in public review; Gowanus Canal projects underway
reporting_angles: Cross-reference 311 complaints with DOB permit filings to identify which projects are generating violations
Interview DOB inspectors on whether new enforcement push or genuine spike in illegal use/conversions
Investigate affordable housing impact: are zoning changes driving illegal conversions to compensate for housing shortage?

themes_detail.label: Derelict Vehicles Problem Worsening
themes_detail.summary: Derelict vehicle complaints reached 15 last week, a 253% increase from the 4.2 weekly baseline (z-score: 4.97), indicating a sustained parking enforcement or vehicle abandonment crisis affecting Park Slope/Carroll Gardens over the past 2 weeks, in a district already drowning in 3,434 illegal parking complaints over 90 days.
evidence: 15 derelict vehicle complaints filed LAST WEEK vs. 4.2 weekly baseline over prior 8 weeks
Z-score of 4.97 indicates statistically significant anomaly
253% increase follows pattern of broader parking crisis: 3,434 illegal parking complaints over 90 days (highest category by volume)
Spike persists as separate signal from baseline illegal parking epidemic
reporting_angles: Interview NYPD Parking Enforcement and Sanitation on tow capacity and abandonment vehicle protocols
Identify blocks with highest derelict vehicle concentration; interview residents about safety/blight concerns
Investigate whether enforcement gap or economic downturn driving vehicle abandonment
